arXiv:2611.05069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum networks distribute entanglement between distant nodes by combining many short entangled links using local quantum operations. item.title: Decoy-state quantum key distribution with a leaky Mach-Zehnder receiver
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Ryohei Mizusawa, Álvaro Navarrete, Akihiro Mizutani, Kiyoshi Tamaki
arXiv:2611.04539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the security of phase-encoded decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution for a Mach-Zehnder receiver with imbalanced beam splitters and two threshold detectors that leak fine-grained information about the detection patterns. For this, we derive a lower bound on Bob's single-photon contributions and combine it with the decoy-state method and a recent phase-error framework for leaky receivers. The leakage-induced correction to the phase-error rate is independent of channel loss, providing a loss-tolerant treatment of receiver leakage even in the presence of beam-splitter imbalance. Our results provide a practical route toward loss-tolerant security proofs for imperfect QKD receivers in the presence of receiver leakage.

arXiv:2611.05233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computers run millions of logical cycles to perform quantum error correction (QEC). item.title: Unital qubit channels are 3-noisy
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Indu Bala, Preeti Parashar, Swapan Rana
arXiv:2611.03894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.
